utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Prosecution ready to continue examination of Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Usher, would you please be so kind to bring Mr. Treanor into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although it might sound as a routine, of course, it never will be a routine when I remind you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm getting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you--

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the wrong language here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you're still on 0 instead of 4. Is that ... Yes. Mr. Treanor, I said that although it might sound as a routine, of course, it never could be a routine when I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You made at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, if I might address the Court briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I gave some consideration to the Court's comments yesterday and to the possibility of adopting an approach that might move us more expeditiously through this process. In that connection, I wanted to note that in addition to selecting documents from an enormous mass of material to be identified for the Court, Mr. Treanor also identified segments or highlights of those documents which merit particular attention and should be brought to the particular attention of the Court. That process, of course, should be used to assist the Court in assessing these large volumes of information. It occurred to me that we might, therefore, move through the highlighted segments that Mr. Treanor has identified in a manner somewhat similar to the fashion that we have approached the intercepts with multiple segments, and that is to move through them serially, to pause at each one in the event that Mr. Treanor wished to make a comment, or alternatively, to run through the entire case of the intercepts, entire clips, in the case of the documents, the entire highlights, and then invite his comments at the end. In that manner, the Court has the benefit of viewing those portions of the document that Mr. Treanor has previously indicated warrant such attention. That will assist the Court not only in the process of this examination, but in reviewing the document subsequently, and we will be able to take advantage of the considerable work that Mr. Treanor has invested before assuming the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's one difference between the intercepts and the portions of documents, Mr. Tieger, and that's the following: When we are listening to the intercepts, for those who speak English, the text appears. For those who do not speak English, they can listen to what has been said, and therefore, under these circumstances, we could just ask Mr. Treanor to give his comments. But if we're looking at documents, of course, the Chamber could read usually even more quickly than Mr. Treanor than reads a specific part. So therefore, if it was just for the Chamber, we could -- we could just hear the comment of Mr. Treanor and that would, under normal circumstances, be sufficient, because we can read the text, but the public character of this trial requires that not only the Judges understand what it's all about, but also that those who are following this trial also can understand what it's all about. So therefore, I asked for the specific, I would say, the -- in one or two lines just the main content of that part of a document, without it being read out in total. So I -- of course, the Chamber certainly is assisted by the investment in understanding these documents made by Mr. Treanor and by explaining, but one of my concerns is how we could move forward with such speed that we don't lose any time, and at the same time, a guarantee that the public will be aware what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I share the Court's concern in that regard, Your Honour, and I did not intend to suggest that we would move through the highlighted portions so quickly that they would not be identified in a sufficient manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let's try and see where we get. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Tieger: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, at the conclusion of yesterday's session, you were discussing the October 24th founding session of the Serbian Assembly, and I believe you had reviewed and discussed the introductory remarks of Mr. Krajisnik. If we could move, then, to the next highlighted segment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That can be found on page 38 of the English translation of the October 24th assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we see Mr. Kostic speaking, and you have highlighted the first two -- first three full paragraphs contained on page 39 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Is it my understanding that the Court and others in the courtroom will now be reading these highlighted portions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just move to the right button. I think if we -- if you try to give -- we read it, and at the same time you could give, in very short terms, what this portion is about. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would just like to say that the speaker at this point, according to the -- a correction on the record that I have and another record we have of this session is in fact Mr. Stanko Cvijan, who is the minister for relations with Serbs outside of Serbia of the Republic of Serbia. In his address here, he expresses his support and approval of what the Bosnian Serb delegates are doing and reviews the sufferings of the Serbian people as a whole in the past and the revival of their political fortunes in the present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next clip. Highlighted on screen are the latter two paragraphs. Are those also embraced by the explanation you just provided?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And the Court will note the -- a reference to the genocide committed during World War II in this passage. That will come up later in this session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 44 of the English translation, the next highlighted portion. Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted the last full paragraph of the English translation at page 44. I believe the speaker is Mr. Koljevic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is Mr. Koljevic speaking now, in a -- in fairly lengthy remarks. In this portion, he speaks of the desire of the Bosnian Serbs to create a new Yugoslavia, one that suits them, and notes that even outside of the type of Yugoslavia they have in mind, over at least half a million Serbs will be left outside of that new Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlight is found at page 47 of the English translation. And we'll continue on to page 48. Can you tell us who that speaker is and why you highlighted that portion.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking at this point is Dr. Karadzic. In his remarks, he addresses what he sees as a plan by outside forces, which is indeed coming to fruition, to dissolve Yugoslavia. He makes reference, I think in the previous paragraph -- well, in this paragraph, to the same plans, the same villains, and the same crimes. Again, this is a reference to the genocide during World War II, which he seems to be suggesting is also being planned in the present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that same page, page 48, there are the last three paragraphs of that page, comprising most of that page are also highlighted and if you can explain their significance, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this portion of his speech, Dr. Karadzic in general is saying that the Serbian people now knows its path forward, but emphasises that they have never been the ones to take the first step, that they have, in effect, always responded to moves that were first made by others. I think this is a theme that we have seen in some of the earlier documents where Dr. Karadzic refers to waiting for other people to make the first move and then they will respond to that move as they have already planned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we turn to page 49, the next page of the English translation. You have highlighted the first paragraph of that page. And would you explain its significance, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is more on the theme of the -- theme of the revival of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the historic step to which Dr. Karadzic refers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at this point he is referring to the establishment of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic also refers in this segment to the shattering of last illusions, to discerning between friends and enemies and to the refusal to allow traitors to deliver us into the hands of our enemies. Are these themes that will be repeated in subsequent speeches by Dr. Karadzic and other Bosnian Serb leaders?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think we will see similar thoughts occurring from this point in, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next highlighted segment can be found on page 50 of the English translation. First of all, is this still Dr. Karadzic speaking?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And here he gets back to the theme of the outside forces working for the destruction of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the remainder of the highlighted sections of the founding assembly refer to decisions made during the course of that assembly. If we could --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This session of the assembly made several very important decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at page 77 of the English translation, is that one of the decisions to which you referred?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see the portion in the record that records the election of Mr. Krajisnik as president of the new Assembly, Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This and the other decisions were published in the Official Gazette, which the Assembly also founded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted segment appears beginning at the bottom of page 79 of the English translation and continues onto the first half of page 80. Page 80 is now shown on your screen, Mr. Treanor. If you could explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision on the remaining of the Serbian people of in BH within Yugoslavia, and as you can see in paragraph 1, refers to the composition of the Yugoslavia, that they are anxious to remain within. Basically, the Serbian portions of Yugoslavia. And I would call attention to paragraph 2, which states that this decision comes into force only after being confirmed at the plebiscite to the Serbian people, which we've referred to yesterday, and this Assembly adopted a decision of holding such a plebiscite at this session as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to pages 81 and 82 of the English translation, do we see further decisions made during the course of that assembly?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision on designating representatives for the Serbian people of BH, as we discussed yesterday, pursuant to the actions of the BH Assembly, which the Bosnian Serbs -- of October 15th, which the Bosnian Serb delegates, that is, the SDS and SPO delegates, regarded as being illegal and illegitimate. They were anxious to have their own representatives in various forums. The people they have designated as representatives in the different forums are listed here. I think further down we'll see that Dr. Karadzic is designated as a representative for the SFRY Presidency. Yesterday I referred to the -- one of the resolutions adopted on October 15th by the Bosnian Serb Assembly, which in effect withdrew Bosnian representatives from the federal institutions, including the Presidency. Reference was made yesterday to Mr. Bogicevic, who was the Bosnian member of the Federal Presidency, who attended a session of that body for the last time on, I believe, October the 1st, and thereafter withdrew his participation, in conformity with the resolution adopted on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. October 15th. And it seemed to be the intention here of the Assembly of the Serbian People that Dr. Karadzic, in effect, take his place in the SFRY Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The final highlighted segment of the October 24th founding assembly is found on page 85 of the English translation. In the second half of that page, as Mr. Cancar speaks about the plebiscite, if you could illuminate that, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the portion in the record of the session at which the -- this particular resolution is read out and then put up for adoption. This is the resolution calling for the plebiscite. If we could stop for a minute and go back a bit to paragraph 2, I would call the Court's attention in particular, in paragraph 2 to the quoted portion, which is the question which will be put to people at the plebiscite. You'll recall the decision of the Assembly that we saw earlier about remaining within Yugoslavia that -- and that decision itself was made contingent on its confirmation at the plebiscite, which here is scheduled for the 10th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, that completes the highlighted segments for the founding assembly. Before we move on to the next document, if you have any additional comments about the assembly itself or the context in which it occurred, I invite you to make them; otherwise, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I'll just repeat what I said yesterday. This is an extremely important event in the development of the policy of the leadership of the Serbian Democratic Party. Here we have formed, in effect, the Chamber of the Serbian People, which, as we have seen from previous documents, they had been seeking for over a year. This body has, certainly in their view, much more legitimacy than, for instance, the Serbian National Council, which we referred to, which was formed a year before and which had a rather short-lived and not too eventful existence. This body is composed of deputies to the duly elected Bosnian Assembly, that is, deputies elected in the elections of 1990; therefore, duly elected representatives of that body, unlike, say, the Serbian National Council, which was self-created. And they have announced their intention that -- I don't know if we're going to be showing this document, but they also adopted a resolution on their own founding, that is, the founding of the Assembly, in which they define this new Assembly as the highest representative and legislative organ of the Serbian people in BH. From this point on in the presentation, we will -- for quite some time, we will in effect be moving from session to session of this Assembly, which, from this point on, is the main forum for decision-making by the SDS leadership and the Bosnian leadership -- Bosnian Serb leadership as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document can be found at tab 54, in binder 4. I'm not sure you have that binder, and it may need to be distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, we see on screen a document entitled, "Decision for the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina to remain in the joint state of Yugoslavia," dated 24 October 1991.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- appears to be, and I judge by the Arabic numeral II in the upper left-hand corner, a translation of this decision as it appeared in the Official Gazette of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The first issue of which was published on the 15th of January, 1992. This is basically the same text that we saw in the record of the session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document is found at tab 55. This document now displayed on screen, Mr. Treanor, bears the title, "The Sarajevo SDS order." It bears a date of October 29th, 1991, and the place is Celinac. If you could address its significance, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document reflects instructions which Dr. Karadzic gave at a meeting on the 26th of October, 1991, in Banja Luka, a meeting apparently of the leaders from the Autonomous Region of Krajina. And it reflects his -- some of his concerns at this particular point in time. I would call attention to the highlighted portions which deal with the familiar -- by now familiar issue of mobilisation. In paragraph 8, we see the reference to building licences, again a reflection of their concern about -- I think of their concern about non-Serbs moving into Serb areas, something we've seen before. Reference again to any paramilitary organisations, that is, irregular armed formations, brought under control or disbanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reference to transfer into the territorial army, is that a reference to the territorial army --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a reference to the Territorial Defence, which is the -- one of the mainstays of the Yugoslav defence system. I don't know if I need to elucidate on that, what the Territorial Defence is. That is a reserve force, if I can put it that way, which was organised within each republic on various levels within the republic, responsible -- all units in the republic responsible to a republic Territorial Defence staff which was funded by the Ministry of Defence of the given republic, and the Territorial Defence was organised in units all the way from republic, they had their own regional structure, regional staffs, down to municipal level, and it included mobile units as well as stationary units in particular factories, other institutions, for the site defence of those facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, before leaving that document, first of all, identify the person who signed or sent the fax.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was sent by Mr. Brdjanin, who we have already referred to several times. He was, in fact, the first vice-president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and here he's described as being the coordinator for implementation of decisions. I would draw attention to one other paragraph in the order, simply because it's a concern that comes up in a later document, paragraph number 5, which refers to taking power in public enterprises, et cetera. I think we'll be seeing expressions of concern on Dr. Karadzic's part in a document we'll see very soon in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the record is clear, the highlighted portions include numbers -- enumerated sentences and instructions numbers 1, 2, 8, and 12. Number 1 to form commands and institute permanent watch immediately; number 2, to institute full mobility of the territorial army; number 8, to postpone issuance of building licences, et cetera; and number 12, the excerpt related to the paramilitary formations in the Territorial Defence that you referred to earlier. If we could move, then, to the next document, which is an intercepted telephone conversation which may be found at tab 19 of the intercepts binder. This is a conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And they discuss what they perceive to be the main tasks before them at the present time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you began to identify the reasons for your selection of that intercept before it was played. If you could continue, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we can see here, once again, there are problems restraining -- there appear to be problems restraining the enthusiasm of other people within the SDS, and Mr. Krajisnik identifies as being the main task the smashing of centralism within BH and establishing control by the Serbs over their own territory. The two of them seem to agree that they are -- they have their path marked out and they don't want to be diverted from it by premature or overenthusiastic moves by other people in the leadership.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Before we move on, I was just wondering if it could be clarified what is the actual date of the conversation. Because what appeared on the screen appeared to have a date of the 29th of October, and the hard copy has the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would compare the B/C/S original and the English translation, then you see that the dates are different where -- although I do not speak any B/C/S, where, in the heading, it says a conversation on the 10th of October in English, where the original says the 29th of October. Mr. Tieger, is this a translation error or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was just about to identify that discrepancy and ask the witness if that was simply a typo in the transcription from B/C/S to English, or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about all I can say is that in my copy of the B/C/S, it says the 29th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the context, Mr. Treanor, do you have any reason to think that the B/C/S date, or the -- is incorrect and that the English translation -- or that the date appearing in the English translation is anything other than a typographical error?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point I don't have any reason to believe that it's anything other than the 29th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if we could move next to a speech given by Dr. Karadzic in November of 1991, entitled, "Plebiscite of the Serbian people."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a speech which I believe in fact was given on the 31st of October, which was a Thursday, at a meeting which we know took place from various diaries we have at 4.30 in the afternoon in the Holiday Inn in Sarajevo. It was a meeting related to plebiscite issues. And internal evidence in the document indicates that it was given before the 1st of November, and there are references to certain television appearances and whatnot that took place around the time we're referring to, the very end of October. And as I say, the diaries indicate that there was a meeting related to this topic on the afternoon of the 31st. So I believe that the speech was given then. In the speech, Dr. Karadzic addresses the general situation within BH and then moves on to address particular issues in connection with the plebiscite and the conducting of the plebiscite. Present at the meeting, from internal evidence, are municipal officials from around BH. Whether they are both party and state officials isn't specified, but I would presume so, and there would include state officials from the municipalities in which the SDS was in power and party officials, at least from those in which it was not in power, but anyways, the people who were going to be responsible for conducting the plebiscite on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the members of the Chamber seem to be aware, this is found at tab 56 of binder 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if we could move to the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one thing, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, at least I've been provided also with the CD-ROM on which it seems that most of these documents appear, but I can find some of them on the basis of the numbers on the bottom or on the top of the page. But some of them, I can't find on that CD-ROM. I don't know how the numbering is done. But, for example, the document under tab 56, I see on the bottom 0027 and then 0630. But I can't find that on my CD-ROM, and I think it's a very helpful instrument if you -- some of the other documents I could find. For example, the transcript of the telephone conversation we just listened to. I find that in the numerical order as it appears on the index, but ... Could someone guide me how to find 55 and now 57?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have a key with me at the moment that would permit me to answer that specific question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could prepare that perhaps during the next break, because some of them, they're quite easily to be retrieved, where others -- for example, here, 57, I find no numbers that give me a clue where to find it on the CD-ROM. Please proceed, and we'll solve the matter during the next break, I take it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if we could move to the first highlighted segment, which is a sentence contained -- or it's the portion of the third full paragraph on the first page which begins, "This is Broz's legacy."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What is important here is, in particular, the sentence about the Muslim brothers, which indicates Dr. Karadzic's attitude, something of his attitude toward them at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted segment appears in the first paragraph of page 4 of the English translation and begins: "I am kindly asking you, I have seen it not only in Krajina but also in Pale, you should seize power completely and energetically."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here's a reference to the point that I mentioned Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. earlier in the -- we saw in the 29 October fax. Here he's referring to the -- his perception that in the municipalities that the SDS controls, they haven't gone far enough in putting their own people into the various positions, in particular, in public enterprises that those municipalities control. He seems to think there are too many holdovers from the communist period who are not loyal to the SDS and that sort of thing, and therefore enjoins his people, as in the 29 October fax, of his instructions of the 26th of October, to address themselves to this area, as he puts it here, to seize power completely and energetically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 5 of the English translation. The first highlighted segment is the fourth paragraph of that page, which begins: "There is a chance that we will fight. In that case, let the chips fall where they may."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this portion, Dr. Karadzic refers to his belief that the Serbs are better armed than their opponents and makes remarks as to what he foresees could be the consequences should hostilities actually break out in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he -- he indicates that no one could stop the almost half a million soldiers who could be mobilised and armed?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it says that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted segment is found in the last paragraph of that page and continues on to page 6.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here Dr. Karadzic refers to some of the demographic concerns of the Bosnian Serb leadership, in this case, in particular, the influx -- or they perceive to be an influx of immigrants, Muslim immigrants from outside of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one thing: One time it says "immigrants," another time is says "emigrants." Is that a mistake or did you check that? It seems to be more logical in the context that it's about immigrants, but ... You see in the first line of this paragraph, you see "immigrants," whereas on the third line, you see "emigrants."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The original is not extremely legible. Perhaps I should leave that for the break and I could try to identify those words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please then proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we could continue with that highlighted portion on the top of page 6.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we see a reference to the land issue again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that passage, Dr. Karadzic indicates that no Muslim foundations will be laid in Serb areas, whether or not, "Turks are imported, because the first foundations will be blown up and all foundations that are laid will be blown up," is that right?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to the next highlighted segment, which appears in the same page, page 6, and begins: "They are implementing a demographic policy here, but we will be implementing one too, and the whole world will understand that."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is more on the demographic concerns of the Bosnian Serb leadership, the land issue is referred to again and mention is made of a battle for living space and the fear that, within ten years, in BH, the Muslims would have an absolute majority in BH. He also refers to what he perceives as the discrimination that Serbs are subjected to, in employment, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's a reference to the passage where Dr. Karadzic refers to 75 per cent of the doctors are Muslims and 75 per cent of the cleaning women are Serbs?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted segment can be found at page 7. It is the latter part of the third full paragraph, beginning: "But there has to be a little discipline once the policy is established."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is Dr. Karadzic, as party leader, once again, enjoining discipline and hard work on the part of his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated previously he was addressing various municipal leaders, among others. Does he identify for them who the leaders of the Bosnian Serbs are who are working on the project he's describing?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. He singles out his leadership team, if you will, including Mrs. Plavsic, Mr. Koljevic, and Mr. Krajisnik, and the deputies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next highlighted segment can be found on page 8 of the English translation. That appears in the last paragraph of that page and begins: "We no longer need an obsolete type of state," and ends, "But if we don't manage to, the ladies will, excuse the expression, mark our territory like dogs then nothing will come of it."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The theme of this passage is getting control by the Bosnian Serbs of their own territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in connection with control of that territory, does Dr. Karadzic go on to speak about identifying that territory with maps, and can that be found on page 9 of the English translation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here we see a reference, indeed, to maps and the plebiscite. There's a reference to the blue map. Now, I'm not positive which map is being referred to; however, I believe that what is in question here is an ethnographic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina which was produced, I believe, in Belgrade, on the basis of the results of the 1991 census. On that map, the predominantly Serb areas of BH are shown in blue, and the visual impression of the map overall is rather one of blueness. So I believe that's why he describes it here as, "The blue map."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is the highlighted segment that begins: "There will be huge interest in our plebiscite," and in which Dr. Karadzic indicates that he took the blue map to the military and said: "Here is a map for you so that you can -- so that you know where you can spend the night. Wherever it is blue, you can spend the night; in the other parts, there is no staying overnight there," followed by applause?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed, the reference in the previous passage to what is ours is ours is perhaps connected with this, could be put as whatever is blue is ours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next highlighted segment, which begins in the second paragraph of that page and continues to the bottom of the page and on into page 10.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a long discussion of -- to the municipal officials, on how they should conduct themselves, and especially in the area of defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he indicate who the commanders of the towns are?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He describes the presidents, I believe he's referring to the presidents of the municipal assemblies as the commanders of the towns. I'm not quite sure how true that was technically under the Territorial Defence set-up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that passage continues on to the beginning of the next page, page 10.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And here we see, at the end of the previous passage, reference to regionalisation, and here we see a reference to the plebiscite of 1920 in Carinthia. This was an analogy that they frequently use when describing their own plebiscite. In 1920, after the World War I, and in pursuance the various treaties that were concluded after that war, a plebiscite was held among the Slovenes in the Austrian province of Carinthia as to whether they wanted to join Yugoslavia. They voted against joining Yugoslavia and remained in Austria, which Slovene nationalists would say turned out to be to the detriment of their national identity. However, this brings up the use of the word "plebiscite" in connection with the polling that they're going to be taking. As we saw in an earlier document, for instance, Dr. Karadzic telling Mr. Brdjanin that, no, no, we don't need a referendum. A referendum is for people that want to leave Yugoslavia. We're not leaving Yugoslavia. We're staying. And anyways, in a referendum, you need a two-thirds majority. So I think that they deliberately did not call this a referendum, but rather a plebiscite in order to distinguish it from the procedure that was specified in the constitution for changing the boundaries, for instance, of BH, via a referendum that required a two-thirds majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next highlighted segment appears in the first full paragraph of page 10 and begins: "The right is in our hands and so is the factual situation, and the factual situation is that it will be impossible for Izetbegovic to establish his authority in 70 per cent of the territory."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is another indication of the extent of the SDS leadership's claims to BH territory. Yesterday we saw reference to 65 per cent. I think I promised that we'd see that figure again. I think we will, but here we see 70 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next highlight appears further on in the page, at the beginning of the second full paragraph, and discusses the army and the fact that their aims and our aims, according to Dr. Karadzic, coincide 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is reference to the -- what he sees as the strong military position of the Serbs. They have the army behind them, and the Serbs have been asking for weapons for themselves. And as he said, they got themselves a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the final clip of the plebiscite speech can be found on page 11 of the English translation. In the first full paragraph, and begins: "So I am asking you, there are two big jobs, two big tasks," and concludes: "If you look at the map, we have a huge territory in BH, a huge territory."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, here we see the -- two of the themes in the speech joined: First job, get the plebiscite done, and after the plebiscite, get to work on consolidating power in the municipalities that they control. He, in this speech, advised that it wasn't such a good idea right before the plebiscite to get people all excited about the fact that they may be losing their jobs, and this, that, and the other thing, that is, present-day directors and those sorts of officials, and thereby arouse opposition just before the plebiscite, at a time when they want to keep things peaceful and on an even keel and get as large a turnout as possible, but to what until after the plebiscite to carry on with the consolidation of power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the next selection is an intercepted telephone conversation which occurred after the date of the plebiscite but refers to it. Do you want to address the results of the plebiscite before we begin that intercept or after it's played?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me find my report of the plebiscite. I think this would be a good time to do that, indeed. Now, the plebiscite took place, in fact, on the 9th and 10th of November. I think there were various international observers present, that sort of thing. It was a big occasion. The plebiscite was, of course, meant to reinforce the stand taken by the Bosnian Serb Assembly against the decisions carried out against its will of the BH Assembly in relation to the status of BH. The plebiscite and its results got to be a mantra for the Bosnian Serb leadership. In the months to come, they referred continuously to the plebiscite and its results as enjoining on them a particular policy, that is, the remaining of the Serbs of BH within Yugoslavia, a policy mandated by the people. Now, the voting for the plebiscite was carried out in almost every municipality in BH. In fact, every municipality apparently. Voting was done according to -- first of all, according to nationality. Serbs voted separately from non-Serbs. Some non-Serbs did vote. Also people who lived outside of BH but came from BH were permitted to vote. And some people were permitted to vote who were not in fact registered voters in BH but presented ID cards at the polling stations to identify themselves. And they voted as well. In total, 1.162.032 citizens of Serbian nationality voted according to the report of the plebiscite commission dated the 11th of November. Of that total, 1.161.146 voted in favour of the plebiscite question, that is, in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia. And providing that their math is correct, that meant for the benefit of the Court, to spare them the subtraction, that 398 people voted against, and there were 488 invalid ballots. The tally for people of Serbian nationality outside of BH who voted is similar, even more overwhelming. Out of 348.231 people, only two voted against. Similarly, out of 49.342 citizens who were not of Serbian nationality and voted in the plebiscite, a total of 397 voted against and there were 50 invalid ballots. So the plebiscite seemed to provide overwhelming support, certainly among the Bosnian Serbs, for the position adopted by the Assembly, that is, that they would remain within Yugoslavia. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn now to an intercepted telephone conversation --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- which may be found at tab 20 of the intercept binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Excuse me. I want to call your attention to the fact that in the records it's been said that the total of citizens that voted was 1.136.000 and then those that voted yes was 1.161.000. That means 25.000 more -- or the number of the voters. That seems to have been a mistake. Would you please verify that? Has been something that was not well understood by Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly. Just to repeat, Your Honour. The number of citizens of Serbian nationality who voted in the plebiscite according to the report of the plebiscite commission was 1.162.032. The number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: That's a mistake here, because it appears to have been 1.136.000, and now you had said 160 something, so perhaps that's -- there is a written mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm looking at the original documents, so I don't know what might be on the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to repeat for the record, Mr. Treanor: The last clarification you offered indicated 1.162.032 voting total, and the number of voting for the proposition was 1.161.146. These are the citizens of Serbian nationality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: So that has clarified that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I add something to that. I would not have intervened if there would have been no confusion. What Mr. Treanor tells us could be said in one or two lines, that is, that an almost hundred per cent vote in favour by the Serbian voters and in the far smaller number of non-Serbian voters, it was also close to a hundred per cent. Without the details, whether there were 32 invalid votes or 72 invalid votes, of course, is not really something that assists the Chamber. Could we try to concentrate on what the main issue is, the main issue is overwhelming, almost hundred per cent in favour of. That's, I think that assists us. The other parts, as we've seen now, even could lead to a lot of confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Next, Your Honours, is the intercept I referred to earlier, found at tab 20 of the intercept binder, and that is a conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Dukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a conversation which is undated, but described as taking place in November 1991. Now, from internal evidence in the conversation, I believe it took place on or shortly before the 15th of November. The conversation relates to the scheduling of certain meetings in connection with the upcoming session of the -- the 2nd Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People. One of those meetings is a meeting of the Main Board, as you'll see from the clip. Now, at the time this conversation took place, that meeting had not taken place at that part of the point of the conversation. We have a written invitation to that meeting which was issued on the 15th of November. So therefore, I would conclude that this conversation took place before that invitation was sent out, but shortly before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is one of a series of documents, some of the others of which we will be seeing. It was -- I suppose I should have mentioned earlier it was preceded by a conversation between Mr. Dukic and Dr. Karadzic about Mr. Dukic's interest in having a Main Board meeting, and Dr. Karadzic, I believe, says, well, you should talk to Mr. Krajisnik about that since we have an assembly session coming up. To remind the Court, Mr. Dukic was the president of the Executive Committee and one of the jobs of the Executive Committee was to prepare materials for meetings of the Main Board. He refers to the fact that the Main Board hasn't met for over a year. I think by that he means that there has not been a session of the Main Board as such in over a year. I think I referred to that earlier in my testimony, that a lot of the meetings that took place were various groups of individuals meeting in large numbers, and not necessarily a meeting of any particular body. He wants to have a Main Board meeting in preparation for the assembly. He incorrectly states that 50 per cent of the members of the Main Board were members of the Assembly. I think that the number is more like a third. But with that, I can we can move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next two documents you've selected, Mr. Treanor, are a November 20th meeting of the Executive Board and a November 21st meeting of the Main Board. If we could turn to the first, which is found at tab 57 of binder 4.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are minutes of the sixth session of the Executive Board. The interest of this document and the next document, which is a Main Board -- minutes of a Main Board meeting, is we can see the progression of the discussion of matters from the Executive Board to the Main Board, and from there, to the Bosnian Serb Assembly itself, where they were finally adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've highlighted on page 2 of that document a paragraph which is labelled "count 2," and discusses the materials for this third session that were discussed, including the report of the plebiscite, information about the activities regarding regionalisation, and so on.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the materials that have been prepared for the Main Board meeting. Further on in that paragraph, the minutes of the Executive Board note that it was concluded that the Assembly of the Serbian People should make a decision on the proclamation of the constituted, that is, formed, regions, which relates to one of the reports that was -- on regionalisation that was going to be -- that would be put before the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In tab 58 of binder 4, the record of the November 21st, 1991 Main Board session is found.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this -- these minutes do not state which session of the Main Board this was. However, as we just saw in the previous excerpt from the minutes of the Executive Board, this was the third session of the Main Board. I'll just remind the Court: The new Main Board was constituted in July 1991. I'm not sure when they start the numeration of meetings of the Main Board, but even if we begin in July, there hadn't been more than two meetings before that. Mr. Dukic had referred to a period of a year. So certainly it was a fairly rare event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've highlighted the last sentence of page 1, which continues on to the next page and reflects a recommendation by the Main Board that the Assembly -- and then it continues on the next page: "Adopt a decision that all settlements where the Serbs declared themselves in favour of staying in Yugoslavia," and so on. Would you explain that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. This is a recommendation based on the results of the plebiscite. We'll be seeing that decision as it was adopted at the assembly session, which in fact took place the same day, to get a better idea of exactly what that decision is about. Further on in this page we see reference to the recommendation that was made by the Executive Board about -- concerning a decision on the Serbian regions. So in this case, we can see that this decision, as I indicated earlier, a recommendation has moved from the Executive Board to the Main Board, and the Main Board is now passing it on to the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, that is the passage -- or the paragraph that begins: "The Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party in Bosnia and Herzegovina recommends that the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina adopt a decision on the proclamation of Serbian regions." If we could turn, then, to the next document, found at tab 59, the second assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, held on November 21, 1991.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the second session of the Assembly. The main work of this Assembly was to review the results of the plebiscite and hear a report on the results of the plebiscite. It also adopted certain decisions, one of which was in fact a decision on the verification of the Serbian autonomous districts that had been proclaimed. It also adopted a decision on those territories which were to be considered territory of the Federal State of Yugoslavia, as foreseen in the Main Board minutes. It also elected a constitutional commission, or a commission for constitutional questions, of the Assembly, whose task was to draft a constitution for the incipient Bosnian Serb entity, and it elected the various members of that commission, one of whom was Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that session, you've highlighted two sections of an address by Mr. Krajisnik. If we could turn to those quickly. The first is found on page 7 of the English translation and appears immediately after he says: "Ladies and gentlemen," and then says: "I am convinced that these are crucial times for the survival of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I would dare say, even more broadly, when it comes to the Serbian people as such."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This -- his address as a whole deals with the efforts of the Bosnian Serb leadership, the SDS leadership, to preserve the common state of Yugoslavia to keep all the Serbs, or most of the Serbs in BH within the same state as the other Serbs in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second highlighted portion is found at page 12 of the English translation, in which Mr. Krajisnik states: "Traitors and outcasts are the most difficult opponents. We would like to send the following message to all those who falter, or are neutral, weak, or misguided," et cetera. "Today you still have time, tomorrow will be too late."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that comes at the -- almost at the end of his fairly lengthy address.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. Perhaps the Court would wish to break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If this would be a suitable time for you, we'll have a break of 20 minutes. We'll adjourn until 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I think I had two smaller questions, one about, Mr. Treanor, that concerns you: Immigration, emigration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour. The good news is that the same word is used in the B/C/S in both places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a B/C/S word. It is not from the Latin root, immigration or emigration. I would, and the translator, at least at one time, did translate the word as "emigrants," that is, people leaving an area. That's all I can say on that issue. It is the same word used in both places.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the good news, I think you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The bad news is it's emigrants. It seems like it should be immigrants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's rather illogical in the context, you would say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would seem to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can add to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There's a tape of that speech. It was listened to over the break. I am advised but we'll double-check when there's more time, that the person who listened to it heard both words used, the word "emigrant," with an E, used the first time, and the word "immigrant" used the second. I know that's not necessarily a helpful clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the other way around as we read it in the transcript. Because there it starts with immigrant and only in second phase we have emigrant with an E. And the first time it was immigrant with an I. So that even complicates matters. Well, it might not be pivotal for the case as a whole, but if you could clarify the issue even further, that would be great. Because now we've got so many versions. We have one immigrants, emigrants, then we have emigrants, immigrants, and then we have the version in the B/C/S language which two times gives emigrants. It's a bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I agree, and when time permits this afternoon, we'll review it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my second question was about the file numbering on the CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're somewhat handicapped because the -- our technical wizard is sick today, but I believe that -- well, we'll certainly either replace the CD and ensure that all the documents Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that the Court needs are contained in a single CD, or we will modify it to include the documents that don't appear there. I don't think it's a problem, however, with the Court's manipulation of the CD itself. I think it's a problem with the content of the CD, and we're addressing that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because what I noticed, just for your information and for the moment when your technical person has recovered, what I see, that sometimes a number -- for example, in the transcripts of telephone conversation, a number is indicated on the bottom of the page, that number appears on the English translation, but if I find that number on the CD, I find the corresponding B/C/S version of that same telephone conversation. But many of them I cannot find at all. But we'll wait and see, because CDs should assist us and not bother us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Absolutely, and we'll do our best to investigate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's good that you warn us. Let's first check whether --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just got it. I've just got it. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you miss, Mr. Krajisnik, what was said before, or was it just a short moment, or was it the whole of the conversation since we started after the break that you missed?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the beginning. But I don't need for any repetition. I will continue listening to the proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll just briefly inform you that we first discussed the issue of emigration, immigration, and the information given to the Chamber was still a bit confusing. And the second thing we discussed was how to find on the CD-ROM that was provided to the Bench the files, because I have some difficulties in finding them. That's what we discussed, nothing else. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you referred earlier to a number of decisions that were made at the second assembly session of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina. If we could run through those very quickly. It may be that no additional comment is necessary, but we should identify those for the record. The first is found on page 21 of the English translation, and it is a decision on the adoption of the report on the plebiscite of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would call attention to paragraph II here. At the end, it indicates that in view of the results of the plebiscite, the decision of the Assembly of the 24th of October, relating to the remaining of the Serbian people of BH within Yugoslavia, is -- has entered into force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second is found at page 25 and is a decision on the municipalities, local communes, and settlements where the plebiscite was held.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision based on the results of the plebiscite, which seeks to define those areas which shall be considered to be the territory of the Federal State of Yugoslavia. At the beginning of the paragraph, we can see that it enumerates municipalities, local communes, and settlements where the plebiscite was held. A settlement is an area even smaller than a local commune. It's the smallest level of census-keeping, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the decision --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: So anywhere where more than 50 per cent of the registered citizens of Serbian nationality in those areas, from a municipality down to a local settlement, are henceforth to be considered part of Yugoslavia. They are part of Yugoslavia, but shall remain part of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, on page 29, the decision on verification of autonomous region appears.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just clarify the previous thing one more time. The reference to municipalities and then the local communes and settlements I believe means that if a particular municipality, as a whole, voted to remain within Yugoslavia, then the whole of that municipality would remain within Yugoslavia. If, however, there should be a local commune or a settlement in a municipality which did not so vote, perhaps because it was a Serbian -- a municipality which was not a Serbian-majority municipality, that the individual settlements and local communes in that municipality would separately be considered as part of Yugoslavia, as opposed to the rest of the territory in that municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred also earlier to the establishment of a constitutional commission and the persons who were selected for membership in that commission. If we could turn quickly to tab 60 and the minutes of the assembly of November 21st. Turn to page 2 of that document. It indicates the membership of the committee continuing on to page 3, where it indicates, as you stated earlier, that Mr. Krajisnik was selected as chairman.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's elected as a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we could turn to page 6 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There he's indicated as chairman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tab 61 of binder 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid, although I'm very much pressed on not to spend unnecessary time on something that -- in the question, you say, Mr. Tieger, that Mr. Krajisnik was selected as the chairman, and the answer was he was elected as a member. And the next question was on page 6, that he's there indicated as a chairman. But on page 2, is he not indicated as a chairman? Or in the beginning of this -- I read on page 2 of the minutes the session was chaired by the President of the Assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik. So it's not an election, but I don't have to go to page 6 to find him as a chairman or -- it's not clear to me what information through the witness you want to present to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, it may be best, Mr. Treanor, if you clarify the appearance of the word "chairman" on page 2 and then the -- its further appearance on page 6.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to find the relevant place in the documentation, without too much success at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to the first page of the minutes first, which is labelled page 2 in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And states that the session was chaired by the President of the Assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik, the chairman stated, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mr. Krajisnik, as president, as we referred to him throughout this testimony, of the Assembly itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we could then turn to page 6 of the English translation, which is a continuation of the listing of the members of the constitutional commission which began on page 5.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this refers to the constitutional commission which is being constituted, if you will, and refers in this place to Mr. Krajisnik as chairman or president of that commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I missed your question. It was also about constitutional commission. So that's my misunderstanding. It also warns me that going too quickly has its disadvantages as well. I apologise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document you've selected, Mr. Treanor, is the 21 November 1991 conclusions. That's found at tab 61. And you've highlighted the paragraph enumerated II, which refers to part of the property from the joint mass media.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This reflects one of the grievances of the Bosnian Serb leadership, that they felt that the media in BH was not objective in reporting on their views and activities, and they were anxious to establish their own media, including radio and television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the second portion of that document you've highlighted appears on page 2, or am I mistaken about that? Well, in any event, if I can direct your attention to the document on the screen at the moment, which is entitled, "Conclusions," and on which you've highlighted the first two paragraphs, I and II.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a resolution adopted in support of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that document is also found at page 61, immediately after the document previously referred to.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reference to defence of the common state, and in I and II, the issue of mobilisation, both of which have been referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document you've selected, Mr. Treanor, is the third assembly session, which was held on December 11th, 1991.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we have skipped a document. We got to the decision on the verification of the autonomous regions, but we never really considered it. I think we went back to revisit an issue. So maybe we should put that up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that document is found at tab 59, on page 29.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the document now on screen the one you were referring to, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By this decision, the Assembly verifies the Serbian autonomous districts, here in the translation referred to as regions that we discussed yesterday. This decision verifies five districts. I mentioned yesterday the formation of six in this decision. Two of the districts, Romanija and Birac, are combined into one district, and the territories of those Serbian autonomous districts are indicated with varying degrees of precision. As the Court will see, for instance, in the first paragraph here relating to the Autonomous Region of Krajina, there are certain whole municipalities which are indicated as being part of that autonomous region. We saw earlier in the documents relating to the formation of the Community of Municipalities and the autonomous region that various municipalities, basically, the Serbian-majority municipalities, joined those bodies. But then it goes on to refer to parts of other municipalities from this region with a majority Serbian population. So here we see the autonomous regions expanding beyond the borders of the original municipalities which joined them. And similar wording is found in the definition of the territory of the other Serbian autonomous regions. Paragraph II of this decision, not surprisingly, defines the autonomous regions as being within BH, as federal units in the common state of Yugoslavia. The wording is a bit confusing. It seems to state that the autonomous districts are themselves federal units within Yugoslavia, on the one hand, but on the other hand, it says that they are part of BH, which of course is still technically itself a federal unit within Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to the 3rd assembly session held on December 11th, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, that can be found at tab 62.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the first two portions of that assembly session that you have highlighted are -- refer to Mr. Krajisnik's explanation of the difference between establishing assemblies in minority municipalities and regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you wanted to guide us to page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. This is precisely right.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I get into that, I'd like to briefly say that this 3rd session held on the 11th of December considered various issues which help to push forward the process of forming a separate Serbian entity in BH. One of them is a recommendation for the foundation of new Serbian municipalities in BH, which we'll be discussing further. There was also a report made on the matter of choosing a prime minister designate for the entity being formed, someone who would be responsible for forming what they refer to as a Council of Ministers. Now, the discussion that Mr. Krajisnik is participating at this point is -- relates the agenda item on the resolution relating to the founding of Serbian municipalities. There was some confusion about this matter among the deputies, and he is trying to explain it to them exactly where Serbian municipalities might be formed and assuring them that this is a separate issue from that of the regionalisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the second highlighted portion which appears on page 22 and 23. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is his remarks on the same topic, I think it's a continuation of the first passage. He's explaining to them that the issue here in these two passages relates to municipalities in which the Serbs are not in the majority, and where they are subject to what he refers to as majorisation, that is, outvoting. In other words, in the Municipal Assembly, since they are not a majority, they can be outvoted and decisions can be taken by that Municipal Assembly that would not be -- that would be contrary to the interests of the Serbian people. So it's within those municipalities that he is saying that new, separate Serbian municipalities should be formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that portion of the highlight ends on page 23, with the sentence: "This is not in collision with regionalisation." Can we turn quickly, then, to the conclusions -- or excuse me, the decisions made or recommendations made at that session. That can be found at tab 61 and appears on screen at the moment entitled, "Recommendation on establishing Municipal Assemblies of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this resolution is framed as a recommendation. Mr. Krajisnik is explaining to the deputies that it was only a recommendation. Some of them had expressed the concern that, in certain areas, it might not be such a good idea to do this. So they didn't want to be bound by any such decision. Some of the deputies had the hope of reaching agreement with the other parties in their particular areas, and thereby keeping the whole of the municipality within Yugoslavia. And they felt that a -- some sort of order to them, instruction to them to split the municipality would be in fact contrary to the Serbian interests in that area. So this is framed as a recommendation to the Deputies' Clubs of the SDS within Municipal Assemblies where they do not have a majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could ask the Chamber to turn back to tab 62. If we can look again at the record of the session and view quickly the portions of that session that you highlighted, the first of which appears on page 19.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mr. Milosevic, who is identified as the president of the Executive Committee of the municipality of Novi Grad, which is one of the Sarajevo municipalities, and he's in favour of this proposal of forming Serbian municipalities as a solution to the problem of immigration, which has resulted in the Serbs becoming a minority in that particular municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that passage, you refer specifically to the influx over the past ten years of between 40.000 and 50.000 of people from Sandzak?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although you've indicated previously the ethnicity of the people from Sandzak, perhaps you can remind us again.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can only assume that the reference here is to Muslims from Sandzak, which is a part of Serbia adjoining Bosnia and Herzegovina on the east, which is heavily populated by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next portion of that session that you've highlighted, Mr. Treanor. That can be found at page 25. It's Mr. Vojo Kupresanin speaking, and the highlighted portion is the second paragraph -- second and third paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To remind the Court: Mr. Kupresanin is not only a deputy in the Assembly, but he is the president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and here he is speaking in favour of the formation of Serbian municipalities. The point that he addresses here is that the Serbs in particular municipalities inhabit extensive portions of the municipality geographically, although from the point of view of overall population, they do not form a majority, due to the concentration of the Muslim population in the towns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the later portion of his address, shortly thereafter, does he make his point even more emphatically?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here is another reference to living space, which we saw Dr. Karadzic referring to in the run-up to the plebiscite. Fear that their living space is being endangered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is the portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one question in respect of the previous part. It reads - but perhaps that's a wrong understanding - "That the plebiscite has shown us accurately which territory is ours," and I see that in this -- that the speaker refers to the -- some difference in landownership and number of Serbs living there, sometimes the ownership up to 80 per cent, 70, 80 per cent, whereas perhaps the number of Serbs is not a majority of the population. Did the plebiscite indicate - and that's not clear to me - anything about landownership? Those who were voting, did they report on their landownership?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not that I'm aware of. What the reference is to, I believe, is the fact that the plebiscite was taken and the results tabulated on the basis of not only the municipality as a whole, but also the local communes and populated places within municipalities. What he seems to be saying here is that on the basis of the results of the plebiscite, they can see which of those settlements and local communes in the municipalities which are -- which have non-Serb majorities are inhabited by Serbs and therefore should be their territory. The -- and he seems to be saying that the total area of those particular local communes in populated places, since they are rural constituencies, if you will, comprise 80 per cent of the territory of Bosanska Krupa, in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. Thank you for clarification. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And just to clarify for the record, the last portion, highlighted portion, from Mr. Kupresanin, to which you referred, is the third paragraph from the bottom, in which he says: "I personally think that our living space and territory is endangered," and the last sentence of which is: "Actually, we have to prevent Muslims from moving into our territories and regions."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. This is a reflection of the concern that we've seen many times already in the course of this presentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next section that you've highlighted and to which I believe you referred earlier is found at page 34.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this -- these remarks are made by Mr. Miskin in the course of a different point of the discussion, a different point of the agenda, which is reports from various bodies on their activities. To remind the Court: Mr. Miskin is the head of the SDS regionalisation staff. So he gives a report on that issue, but he makes a few general recommendations and remarks as well, one of them being his belief that the formation of a Council of Ministers as soon as possible would assist in the matters that he's concerned with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the third paragraph, which is a single sentence, from the bottom of page 34. Turning to the next page, as Mr. Miskin continues, you've highlighted a portion there, which is the fourth full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here he addresses the issue of defence and the need for contingency plans in that connection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the final segment that you've highlighted, Mr. Treanor, is found at page 48, continuing on to page 49. And that is an address by Velibor Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
